subject: Staged usage engagement: structured commit options and breakpoint calculations
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acme-fin.tech>; procurement@acme-fin.tech
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Staged usage engagement: structured commit options and breakpoint calculations

Hi Sara / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning — appreciate the clarity on projected Q1 usage. Per follow-up, I attached a concise proposal with three annual commit profiles aimed at balancing unit pricing, carryover flexibility, and predictable capacity: Starter, Growth, and Enterprise. High-level summary below (see attached commit_pricing_v2.xlsx for exact per-token math and breakpoint examples):

- Starter: 500k tokens/year — best for pilot workloads. Base: $0.012/token; no tiered breakpoints. 30-day carryover for unused tokens.
- Growth: 5M tokens/year — predictable ramp for production. Base: $0.009/token with breakpoints at 2.5M (5% off) and 5M (10% off). 6-month carryover.
- Enterprise: 50M tokens/year — committed capacity with tighter SLAs. Base: $0.0065/token with breakpoints at 25M (12% off), 50M (20% off). 12-month carryover + dedicated routing and 99.9% uptime SLA.

Two important commercial levers we can customize: staged breakpoints (so pricing steps up/down based on actual monthly burn) and onboarding credits for the first 3 months (one-time) to cover migration/integration token consumption.

Ask: can you confirm (1) the expected model mix (e.g., majority gpt-4-style open model vs embeddings heavy), and (2) whether carryover is acceptable (we can tighten for procurement if needed)? If you’re comfortable, I’ll circulate a proposed SOW + finalized pricing table we can put into DocuSign.

Attachments: commit_pricing_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-token math and worked examples), draft_sow_acme.docx (SOW skeleton).

Next step: propose 30-minute pricing + legal sync on Thursday at 10am PT. Happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Marcus — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions from procurement/legal before we route to our budget committee:

1) Effective blended per-token rate examples: can you provide a worked example for a 40M burn year under the Enterprise plan (showing the blended $/token after breakpoints)?
2) Carryover: we generally prefer shorter carry windows. Is there flexibility to reduce Growth carryover to 3 months in exchange for a slightly higher minimum commitment?
3) Termination / IO: what are the standard termination-for-convenience notice and refund mechanics for unused prepaid tokens?
4) SLA: can you confirm target MTTR for regional incidents and the escalation path?

We can join a quick call Thursday; procurement would like the finalized numbers and a sample SOW in advance.

Regards,

Director, Cloud Procurement
Acme Financial

Cc: procurement@acme-fin.tech, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Staged usage engagement: structured commit options and breakpoint calculations

Sara — thanks, good questions. Short answers up front, followed by the attached worked example: commit_pricing_v2.xlsx has line-item math; pasted examples here for quick review.

1) Blended example (Enterprise) — 40M annual burn:
   - Breakpoint tiers: 0–25M @ $0.0065, 25M–50M @ $0.00572 (12% off list), 50M+ @ $0.0052 (20% off list)
   - Calculation: (25M * $0.0065) + (15M * $0.00572) = $162,500 + $85,800 = $248,300 -> blended $/token = $248,300 / 40,000,000 = $0.0062075 (~$0.00621/token)

2) Carryover flexibility — we can do Growth carryover = 3 months if Acme moves minimum annual commit from 5M -> 6M. That trade preserves forecastability for capacity planning.

3) Termination & refunds — standard: 60-day notice for termination-for-convenience on annual commits. Unused prepaid tokens: refundable in cash if requested during a 90-day post-termination settlement window at a 75% refund rate (reflects provisioning and capacity impacts). We can table alternative language for Enterprise with negotiated carve-outs.

4) SLA & MTTR — Enterprise tier includes 99.9% uptime, 2-hour critical incident response, primary on-call escalation to our SRE director, and monthly availability reports. We will include a regional MTTR objective in the SOW; SLA credits are pro-rated token credits up to agreed caps.

I’ve attached an updated spreadsheet (commit_pricing_v2.xlsx) with the blended-example tab and a draft SOW (draft_sow_acme.docx). Also added a HubSpot deal link and a placeholder DocuSign envelope. If those numbers look good, Marissa can finalize the first-year onboarding credit proposal (we typically offer 5–10% of the first-year commit as token/top-up credits; may be applied as a one-time credit within the first billing cycle).

If you confirm willingness to move Growth -> 6M for 3-month carryover, I can circulate an updated quote within 48 hours. Otherwise, we’ll keep Growth at 5M with the original 6-month carryover.

Best,
Marcus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staged usage engagement: structured commit options and breakpoint calculations

Quick internal — ran margin back-of-envelope with finance: the Enterprise blended example (~$0.0062/token @40M) keeps healthy gross margin given reserved pools, but offering a 10% first-year onboarding credit drops effective yield meaningfully. Recommend we offer up to 7% onboarding credit OR a one-time $50k implementation credit for Acme.

Also confirm we can include 99.9% uptime + 2-hour critical response in the SOW for Enterprise. Ben: can you confirm whether the 60-day termination and 75% refund for unused tokens is acceptable from billing/legal?

- Marissa
